title: Opening Drive
teaches: The opening drive as we trade it: the day-1 entry for a leader above its 200-day, read on 5-minute bars. The first 5-minute bar closes green, the day's low is the open or inside that bar, and price never trades back to the open; the buy is a market order the moment price trades through the first bar's high, never more than 4% past it; the stop sits a few cents under the day's low; a third comes off at 3R and 5R with the rest on the trail; a stop-out is the plan working, and the second entry is the first light-volume pullback that holds VWAP.

facts.quote: A stock gaps up or down on earnings and drives strongly in one direction during the first few minutes of the Open.
facts.claim: SMB: after a gap on news, the stock drives strongly in one direction in the first few minutes.

facts.quote: Let’s define what we mean by an Opening Drive Play. This is a momentum trade right on the open, right after 9:30AM.
facts.claim: SMB: the Opening Drive Play is a momentum trade right on the open, right after 9:30.

facts.quote: Generally when there is going to be a good opening drive it happens right away.
facts.claim: SMB: a good opening drive happens right away.

facts.quote: It is unusual for there to be a delay of 5-6 minutes.
facts.claim: SMB: a delay of 5 to 6 minutes before a drive is unusual.

facts.quote: With an Opening Drive Play we do not let the stock trade back down against us.
facts.claim: SMB: with an Opening Drive Play, we do not let the stock trade back down against us.

facts.quote: On the open we trade the momentum. We do not trust trends in the first 30 minutes. The best play on the open is the Opening Drive.
facts.claim: SMB: on the open we trade momentum, not trends; the best play on the open is the Opening Drive.

facts.quote: You are either in a Scalp Opening Drive Play with all its specific exits or a Trade2Hold Opening Drive Play.
facts.claim: SMB: you are in a scalp or a hold plan, chosen before the entry.

facts.quote: you almost never want to start a Trade2Hold on the open because stocks do not trend on the open
facts.claim: SMB: stocks do not trend on the open, so a hold plan almost never starts there.

facts.quote: You should see a price surge and elevated volume right after the opening bell rings.
facts.claim: SMB: a drive shows a price surge and elevated volume right after the bell.

facts.quote: After a strong Opening Drive, we want to see a pull in on light volume, and a hold above VWAP.
facts.claim: SMB: after a strong drive, the pullback is on light volume and holds above VWAP.

facts.quote: Be careful about confusing an opening drive for a stock trending
facts.claim: SMB: do not confuse an opening drive for a stock trending.

facts.quote: use the retracement high/low as a price to place your stop
facts.claim: SMB: for the pullback entry, place the stop at the retracement low.

facts.claim: Zarattini et al.: the first 5-minute candle sets the direction; a bearish one means short only, so a bullish one means long only.

questions.q: On our drive card, which bar's high is the buy point?
choices: The first 30-minute bar's high
The prior day's high
The opening print
The first 5-minute bar's high
questions.why: The first 5-minute bar's high, called the 5-minute ORH (opening range high). The buy is the trade through it. The 30-minute range is the slow version, the ORB.
questions.lesson_line: Mark the first 5-minute bar's high. The buy is the trade through it.

wrong.The first 30-minute bar's high: That is the ORB's range, the slow version of the same day.
wrong.The prior day's high: That is a Kicker entry. The drive reads the first bar of its own day.
wrong.The opening print: The open is one price. The drive needs a bar's high.

questions.q: In a true opening drive, the day's low comes late, well after the first 30 minutes.
questions.why: False. The drive is over in minutes: the day's low is the open or inside the first 5-minute bar. SMB Capital, the desk that named the play, calls it a momentum trade right on the open.
questions.lesson_line: A real drive makes its low in the first bar and never looks back.

questions.q: You are filled on the drive. Where does the stop go?
choices: Under the 50-day average
A few cents under the day's low
Exactly on the first bar's low
Just under the prior close
questions.answer: A few cents under the day's low
questions.why: A few cents under the day's low, which in a true drive is the first bar's low or the open. Kullamagi's stop is at the lows of the day too.
questions.lesson_line: Stop under the day's low, not on it. In a true drive that low is the first bar or the open.

wrong.Under the 50-day average: That is far below. The drive's stop is the day's low.
wrong.Exactly on the first bar's low: The stop sits a few cents under the low, not exactly on it.
wrong.Just under the prior close: That sits below the whole gap, a far wider stop than the day's low.

questions.q: Tap the number that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: Never fill a drive more than ___% above the first 5-minute bar's high.
questions.why: 4%. Past 4% above the first bar's high the buy point has passed. Chasing costs size, not risk: the stop stays put and the distance grows.
questions.lesson_line: Four percent past the first bar's high and the buy point is gone. Use the second entry.

questions.q: We wait for a 5-minute bar to close above the first bar's high, then buy.
questions.why: False. We buy at market the moment price trades through the first bar's high, with no waiting for the bar to close. Breitstein does not wait for bar closes either.
questions.lesson_line: The trade through is the trigger. A close is a report, not a signal.

questions.q: The prior close is under the 200-day. The first bar is green on big volume. Our rule?
choices: No long; below the 200-day
Buy it; the volume overrides
Buy at half size
questions.why: No long. We take no longs below the 200-day simple moving average, unless it is a parabolic long. A big green first bar does not change that.
questions.lesson_line: Under the 200-day there is no drive to buy. Volume does not buy an exception.

wrong.Buy it; the volume overrides: A hard rule has no volume exception. The 200-day comes first.
wrong.Buy at half size: A hard rule has no half size. Under the 200-day there is no long.

questions.q: We take drives in leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in a strong group.
questions.why: True. We buy leaders: an RS rating of 80 or more, in one of the strongest groups.
questions.lesson_line: Drives belong to leaders. RS 80 or more, in a strong group.

questions.q: At 9:36 price ticks a cent over the first bar's high. The 9:35 bar has not closed. Do you buy?
choices: Yes; the trade through is the trigger
No; wait for the 9:35 bar to close
No; wait for three closed bars
Yes, but only with a limit order
questions.answer: Yes; the trade through is the trigger
questions.why: Yes. The trade through is the trigger, bought at market. We do not wait for a close, and entries are market orders.
questions.lesson_line: A close tells you what already happened. The trade through fires the buy.

wrong.No; wait for the 9:35 bar to close: Waiting for the close is chasing. The card says no waiting for the bar to close.
wrong.No; wait for three closed bars: Three closed bars would leave the drive far behind you. The card buys the trade through.
wrong.Yes, but only with a limit order: Entries are market orders. A limit can miss the break and leave you watching.

questions.q: A good opening drive usually shows itself right away. A delay of 5 to 6 minutes before it starts is unusual.
questions.why: True. SMB Capital: a good opening drive happens right away, and a delay of 5-6 minutes is unusual. Our card buys over the first bar's high by about 9:40.
questions.lesson_line: A good drive starts right away. A long wait before it starts is unusual.

questions.q: The first 5-minute bar closes green but trades under its normal volume. What is it?
choices: A drive with a wider stop
A B-grade drive
Not a drive
A drive at half size
questions.why: Not a drive. First 5-minute volume under its average fails the card. Zarattini et al. found the 5-minute break averaged -0.02R below 100% relative volume.
questions.lesson_line: A green bar with no crowd behind it is not a drive.

wrong.A drive at half size: There is no half-size drive. Under its average volume it is not a drive at all.
wrong.A drive with a wider stop: A wider stop on a non-drive only adds risk.
wrong.A B-grade drive: B grades still have the volume. Under the average is a no-trade.

questions.q: Tap the word that fits the blank.
questions.sentence: A drive day that closes in the ___ third of its range has failed.
questions.why: Bottom. A drive day that closes in the bottom third of its range, or below its open, has failed. It is a warning: the stop is the only exit.
questions.lesson_line: Where the day closes grades the drive. The bottom third is a failed one.

questions.q: A drive fires on the earnings gap day, after the report. Is the earnings rule a problem?
choices: No; the report is behind it
Yes; no buys on a report day
Yes; wait 3 sessions first
questions.answer: No; the report is behind it
questions.why: No. The blackout is the 3 sessions before a report. A drive on the earnings gap day comes after the report, so it is allowed.
questions.lesson_line: The earnings rule looks forward. Once the report is out, the drive is allowed.

wrong.Yes; no buys on a report day: The blackout is before the report. The day after it, the drive is allowed.
wrong.Yes; wait 3 sessions first: The 3 sessions are before a report, not after. Nothing makes you wait afterwards.

questions.q: After you are filled on a drive, you can widen the stop if the stock dips.
questions.why: False. The stop is a real order with the broker and only rises after entry. The one exception is the gap rule.
questions.lesson_line: The stop only moves up. A stop you widen is a stop you stopped believing.

questions.q: Which market reading gives full risk on a drive?
choices: Orange
Red
Green
Yellow
questions.why: Green. Green is full risk, Yellow is smaller and fewer, Orange is A+ only, and Red is mostly cash.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market before the stock. Green is full risk; Red is mostly cash.

wrong.Yellow: Yellow means smaller and fewer, not full risk.
wrong.Red: Red is mostly cash, plus shorts below the 200-day.

questions.q: The first 5-minute bar runs 272.80 to 277.23. You fill at 277.24 with the stop at 272.75. How far below the fill is the stop, in percent?
questions.why: 1.62%. The fill minus the stop, divided by the fill. That is LRCX: a tight first bar gives a close stop, well inside the 3% a stop usually sits within.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last. A tight first bar makes a close stop.

questions.q: A buy fires at 10:05 over the 9:30 to 10:00 high. Which setup is it?
choices: An opening drive
A Kicker
An ORB
questions.why: An ORB. It waits for the full 9:30 to 10:00 range and buys the first trade through its high after 10:00. A drive is bought over the first 5-minute bar's high by about 9:40.
questions.lesson_line: Check the clock. A buy near 9:40 over the first bar is the drive; after 10:00 it is the ORB.

wrong.An opening drive: A drive is bought over the first 5-minute bar's high by about 9:40. This one waited for 10:00.
wrong.A Kicker: A Kicker needs a real red day before the gap. Nothing here says that.

questions.q: If the stock loses VWAP and holds under it before your entry, you still buy at half size.
questions.why: False. Losing VWAP and holding under it means the drive has failed. Before the entry, that is no trade; after it, a warning.
questions.lesson_line: VWAP lost before you buy is a pass. VWAP lost after you buy is a warning.

questions.q: Your drive is up 2R by noon. By the hard rule, when does the first third come off?
choices: At 5R
At the close
At 3R
At 2R
questions.why: At 3R. The hard rule is a third at 3R, another third at 5R, and the last third on the trail.
questions.lesson_line: A third at 3R, a third at 5R, and trail the rest. The R tells you, not the clock.

wrong.At 2R: 2R is inside the range where the stop may move to breakeven. The first trim is 3R.
wrong.At the close: There is no time-of-day sale. The trim is a price.

questions.q: On a drive the stop moves to breakeven between 2R and 5R, at the first trim by default.
questions.why: True. Breakeven comes between 2R and 5R, and by default at the first trim, which is a third at 3R.
questions.lesson_line: Take the first third at 3R and the stop goes to breakeven. Free trade, not a free pass.

questions.q: A drive in a $7 stock that trades $12 million a day is fine if the first bar is clean.
questions.why: False. We trade only stocks at $10 or more that trade at least $20 million a day. A clean first bar does not fix the liquidity.
questions.lesson_line: Liquidity is a gate, not a grade. Under $10 or $20 million a day is out.

questions.q: Fill 581.57, stop 572.82. Where is 3R?
questions.why: 607.82. One R is the fill minus the stop; add three of those to the fill. SITM got there at 9:50 the same day.
questions.lesson_line: Know your 3R before the open. The first third comes off there.

questions.q: Kullamagi picks the stock on the daily chart first and uses the open only to time the buy.
questions.why: True. Kullamagi says to look at the daily chart and enter when the stock starts to break out. The opening range high times the entry; the stop is at the lows of the day.
questions.lesson_line: Pick the stock on the daily chart. The open only times the buy.

questions.q: The first 5-minute high is 71.99. You look up and the stock trades 75.00. How far above the high is that, in percent?
questions.why: 4.18%, past the 4% line. The buy point has passed. Chasing costs size, not risk, so the second entry is the only entry.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the chase before you buy it. Past 4%, the first pullback is the way in.

questions.q: What now?
questions.story: You looked away. At 9:41 the stock is 5% above the first bar's high and still climbing.
choices: Pass; wait for the first pullback
Buy now; momentum is the proof
Buy half size to stay involved
Short it; 5% up is overextended
questions.answer: Pass; wait for the first pullback
questions.why: Pass and wait for the first pullback. Past 4% the buy point has passed. The second entry is a pullback on lighter volume that holds VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: Missed it means missed it. The pullback that holds is the next trigger.

wrong.Buy now; momentum is the proof: Past 4% above the first bar's high is a chase. Our rule says never.
wrong.Buy half size to stay involved: Half of a chase is still a chase. Size does not fix the distance to the stop.
wrong.Short it; 5% up is overextended: Fading a strong leader is fighting the trend we came to buy.

questions.q: Is the drive still on?
questions.story: You have not bought yet. The first bar closed green on heavy volume. At 9:42 price trades 10 cents under the open.
choices: Yes; ten cents is just noise
Yes; buy the dip
Yes; take it with a wider stop
No; it failed the open-test
questions.why: No. Once price trades back below the open before the entry, it is an open-test or a rejection, not a drive. No trade.
questions.lesson_line: A drive does not look back. Under the open before you buy, you pass.

wrong.Yes; ten cents is just noise: SMB: we do not let the stock trade back down against us. Under the open is the line crossed.
wrong.Yes; buy the dip: A dip under the open before the entry is the failure, not a discount.
wrong.Yes; take it with a wider stop: A wider stop only buys more risk on a drive that failed its test.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: You hold a drive. Two sessions later the stock gaps open below your stop.
choices: Hold; the stop was already passed
Buy more at the lower price
Make the first 30-minute low the stop
Sell at the open and take the loss
questions.answer: Make the first 30-minute low the stop
questions.why: Make the first 30-minute low the stop. A gap through the stop hands it to the first 30 minutes of the gap-down day. If they take the loss past 2R, get out.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide, under a 2R ceiling.

wrong.Hold; the stop was already passed: There is always a stop. The new one is the 30-minute low, and 2R is the ceiling.
wrong.Buy more at the lower price: Full size at one price with one stop, no adding.
wrong.Sell at the open and take the loss: The gap rule gives it the first 30 minutes. The open alone is not the decision.

questions.q: On the second entry, the stop stays under the first bar's low, not the pullback's low.
questions.why: False. For the pullback entry the stop sits a few cents under the pullback's low. SMB uses the retracement low as the stop.
questions.lesson_line: A pullback entry gets its own stop, a few cents under the pullback's low.

questions.q: Two thirds are sold at 3R and 5R. What takes you out of the last third on a fast mover?
choices: A close below the 10-day average
Any dip under the 10-day average
The next red candle
A close below the 50-day average
questions.why: A close below the 10-day average. The default trail is the 10-day for fast movers and the 21-day for steadier ones, sold on a close below it.
questions.lesson_line: Trail the last third on a close under the 10-day, or the 21-day for a steadier stock.

wrong.Any dip under the 10-day average: The trail sells on a close below the line, not a touch.
wrong.The next red candle: A red candle is not the trail. The line is the average.
wrong.A close below the 50-day average: The default is the 10-day for fast movers, the 21-day for steadier ones.

questions.q: A drive still under 1R after ten trading days is sold, to free the money.
questions.why: True. A trade still under 1R after 10 trading days is sold. Money tied up in a stalled trade is not working.
questions.lesson_line: A drive that has not paid in ten sessions has told you something. Sell and move on.

questions.q: Take it as one of our drives?
questions.story: CROX, 2026-09-17: a clean one-bar drive. A 2.2% gap, the first bar closes at 90% of its range, and RS is 77.
choices: Pass; RS 77 is not a leader
Take it; the drive is perfect
Take it at half size
questions.answer: Pass; RS 77 is not a leader
questions.why: Pass. We buy leaders: RS 80 or more. CROX still ran 5.8R at its best, and it is still not ours. A trade that works does not change the rule.
questions.lesson_line: A drive that works is not always our drive. Under RS 80, I pass.

wrong.Take it; the drive is perfect: The shape was perfect and the rank was not. Leaders first, then the shape.
wrong.Take it at half size: A hard rule has no half size. RS 77 is under the line.

questions.q: What do we do?
questions.story: ONON, 2026-09-22: a 10.2% gap on heavy volume. The stock sits 30% below its 200-day, RS 2, and closes at the low of the day.
choices: Buy the gap; 10% is rare
Buy half size, stop at the low
No trade; it is below the 200-day
questions.answer: No trade; it is below the 200-day
questions.why: No trade. The stock sat far below its 200-day with RS 2, and our 200-day rule keeps us out. It closed at the low of the day.
questions.lesson_line: Heavy volume and a big gap do not cancel the 200-day. Below it, I pass.

wrong.Buy the gap; 10% is rare: A rare gap is not a rule. No longs below the 200-day.
wrong.Buy half size, stop at the low: A hard rule has no half size. Below the 200-day there is no long.

questions.q: Which is too stretched to buy?
questions.story: Two drives. One fills 9.8% over its 10-day average. The other fills 12% over its 10-day average.
choices: The one 12% over
The one 9.8% over
Both
Neither
questions.why: The 12% one. We skip a long more than 10% above its 10-day average. MXL, 9.8% over its 10-day, sat at the edge and ran 5.2R at its best.
questions.lesson_line: More than 10% over the 10-day is stretched. A gap on top of a run can be stretched before it opens.

wrong.The one 9.8% over: That is inside the 10% line, at the edge. It passes the stretch rule.
wrong.Both: Only the one past 10% fails. The other sits just inside.
wrong.Neither: 12% is past the 10% line. It is stretched.

questions.q: A euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 of a parabolic burst is a strong long, because momentum peaks then.
questions.why: False. A euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 of a burst is the short setup. Breitstein's own best-known short ends with a euphoric opening drive.
questions.lesson_line: Count the up days. Day 3 to 5 with a euphoric open is a climax, not a buy.

questions.q: You missed the 9:35 trigger. What is the next entry?
choices: Market-on-close if it holds the high
Tomorrow's open, if it gaps up
A light pullback that holds VWAP
The next green candle over the open
questions.answer: A light pullback that holds VWAP
questions.why: The first light-volume pullback that holds VWAP, bought on the break back over the pullback's high. SMB wants a pull in on light volume and a hold above VWAP.
questions.lesson_line: Missed the drive, wait for the pullback. Light volume, holds VWAP, buy the break back up.

wrong.Market-on-close if it holds the high: The card has no close entry. The second entry is the pullback break.
wrong.Tomorrow's open, if it gaps up: The drive is a morning entry. The second entry is the pullback that holds, not a later open.
wrong.The next green candle over the open: A green candle is not a level. The second entry needs a pullback that holds.

questions.q: A strong group gapping together is a cue that grades a drive higher.
questions.why: True. A strong group gapping together, and big news days when many stocks are in play, are cues. Software did it on 2026-09-14.
questions.lesson_line: One name is a story; a whole group is a tide. Grade the drive up.

questions.q: Two drives on the same daily setup. Which grades higher?
choices: One at a full day's volume by 9:45
One on average first-bar volume
Same; the daily setup is identical
questions.answer: One at a full day's volume by 9:45
questions.why: The one that trades its average daily volume in the first 15 minutes. That is an A+ mark: the average daily volume within the first 15 to 30 minutes.
questions.lesson_line: A stock that trades a full day's average volume before 9:45 is in play.

wrong.One on average first-bar volume: Average volume in the first bar is only the floor. The A+ mark is far heavier.
wrong.Same; the daily setup is identical: Volume grades the drive. Our card marks the heavy one A+.

questions.q: Account 100,000. Risk 0.4%. Fill 208.00, stop 205.66. How many shares?
questions.why: 170. Account times risk percent, divided by the fill minus the stop, rounded down. The stop sets the size, never the other way round.
questions.lesson_line: Stop first, distance second, size last.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: WDC, 2026-10-05: a real drive, but the first bar is 3.6% tall. The honest stop is 3.53% under the 445.63 fill.
choices: Buy full size anyway
Put the stop at the open
Let the stop set the size, or skip
Tighten the stop to keep 1% size
questions.answer: Let the stop set the size, or skip
questions.why: Let the stop set the size, or skip. A wide stop means fewer shares, and if the honest stop does not fit the risk, we skip the trade.
questions.lesson_line: The honest stop sets the size. If it does not fit, skip the trade.

wrong.Tighten the stop to keep 1% size: A tight stop is not a free stop. The stop belongs under the day's low.
wrong.Buy full size anyway: Full size on a wide stop risks more than planned. The stop sets the size.
wrong.Put the stop at the open: The stop is a few cents under the day's low, wherever that is.

questions.q: What did our rules keep?
questions.story: You bought CNC's drive at 72.00, stop 70.16. At 9:35 the next day it prints 3R, 77.52. Two days later it falls back to the old stop.
choices: A full-size loss
A third banked at 3R, the rest near even
Nothing; it round-tripped
Two thirds, sold at 5R
questions.answer: A third banked at 3R, the rest near even
questions.why: A third banked at 3R. The rule is a third off at 3R, with the stop to breakeven by default. Trim a third at 3R or keep nothing.
questions.lesson_line: The first trim turns a round trip into a win. Take the third at 3R.

wrong.Nothing; it round-tripped: The third sold at 3R was already banked. That is why we trim.
wrong.Two thirds, sold at 5R: The stock never reached 5R. Only the first third came off.
wrong.A full-size loss: The stop moved to breakeven at the first trim, so the rest left near even.

questions.q: What does the rulebook say?
questions.story: You bought a drive at 9:35. It closes at 24% of its range, still above your stop.
choices: A warning; the stop is the only exit
Sell at the close to be safe
Sell at tomorrow's open
Hold and add on the next dip
questions.answer: A warning; the stop is the only exit
questions.why: A warning; the stop is the only exit. A drive day that closes in the bottom third has failed, but we do not add an exit the rulebook lacks.
questions.lesson_line: A weak close is a warning, not an order. The stop is the exit.

wrong.Sell at the close to be safe: That adds an exit we do not have. The stop is the only exit.
wrong.Sell at tomorrow's open: Same mistake, a day later. The stop is the only exit.
wrong.Hold and add on the next dip: Full size at one price with one stop, no adding.

questions.q: LRCX's first 5-minute bar dipped first, then closed 63% up its range. Is it a drive?
choices: No; any first-bar dip kills a drive
Yes; it need not close in the top 30%
No; it must close in the top 30%
questions.answer: Yes; it need not close in the top 30%
questions.why: Yes. The first 5-minute bar must close above its open, but it need not close in its top 30%. A drive may dip in the first minute.
questions.lesson_line: Green bar, no trade back to the open. A first-minute dip does not break a drive.

wrong.No; it must close in the top 30%: The card says the first bar need not close in its top 30%. LRCX ran 16.8R.
wrong.No; any first-bar dip kills a drive: A drive may dip in the first minute. What kills it is trading back to the open before the entry.

questions.q: After the first third at 3R, the last two thirds ride the trail with no second trim.
questions.why: False. After the first third at 3R, another third comes off at 5R, then the last third rides the trail.
questions.lesson_line: Thirds at 3R and 5R, then the trail. The plan decides before the stock does.

questions.q: What does that do for a drive?
questions.story: The Nasdaq is trending above a rising 10 and 20-day average, and breadth is strong at the open on a broad gap-up.
choices: It makes the drive rules optional
It means skip drives for the day
It is a cue that grades drives up
questions.answer: It is a cue that grades drives up
questions.why: It is a cue that grades drives higher. The simple market test is the Nasdaq trending above a rising 10 and 20-day average.
questions.lesson_line: A good market lifts the grade. It never loosens a rule.

wrong.It makes the drive rules optional: A cue grades; it does not loosen a rule. Every rule still applies.
wrong.It means skip drives for the day: That is the best backdrop for a drive, not a reason to skip.

questions.q: What is it?
questions.story: NVT, 2026-10-02: a gap-up and a green first bar. At 9:35 price trades back under the 169.59 open. The first bar's high is taken at 9:40.
choices: An open-test; no trade
A drive; buy the 9:40 break
A drive with a late trigger
An ORB
questions.why: An open-test, no trade. The first bar's low was lost before the trigger, so the rule says no trade.
questions.lesson_line: The break at 9:40 does not matter if it went back under the open at 9:35.

wrong.A drive; buy the 9:40 break: Price traded back under the open first. A drive never does that before the entry.
wrong.A drive with a late trigger: The failure is the trade back under the open, not the clock.
wrong.An ORB: An ORB waits for the full 9:30 to 10:00 range. This is a failed drive, not a slow one.

questions.q: Whose rules apply?
questions.story: A leader in a daily setup gaps up 4.7% on heavy first-bar volume. There is no named catalyst and the name is not neglected.
choices: The opening drive's
An Episodic Pivot's
A Kicker's
questions.why: The opening drive's. An EP needs a gap of 10% or more on a named catalyst in a neglected name. A leader with a smaller gap and no news is a drive.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the gap and name the news. Ten percent and a catalyst is an EP; a leader with less is a drive.

wrong.An Episodic Pivot's: An EP needs a gap of 10% or more on a named catalyst in a neglected name. 4.7% with no news is not that.
wrong.A Kicker's: A Kicker needs a real red day before the gap. Nothing here has one.

questions.q: Whose rules win?
questions.story: A Kicker is on the focus list: a real red day, then a gap up. The stock drives straight up from the 9:30 bell.
choices: The drive's, with the day's-low stop
Neither; skip it
The Kicker's, with its stop cap
questions.answer: The Kicker's, with its stop cap
questions.why: The Kicker's. A Kicker that drives from the bell is both setups, and the Kicker's rules, including its 3.5% stop cap, win.
questions.lesson_line: When two setups fit, the Kicker's rules win. Its stop cap comes first.

wrong.The drive's, with the day's-low stop: The Kicker's rules win when it drives from the bell, stop cap included.
wrong.Neither; skip it: A Kicker that drives is a valid trade. It just follows the Kicker's rules.

questions.q: Long or short setup?
questions.story: Three straight up days and two overnight gap-ups, with growing candles. On day 4 it gaps again and drives hard from the bell on a euphoric open.
choices: A drive at half size
The U-Turn short setup, not a long
A drive; buy the 5-minute high
questions.answer: The U-Turn short setup, not a long
questions.why: The U-Turn short setup, not a long. A euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 of a burst, with growing candles, is the climax. It belongs to the Parabolic Short.
questions.lesson_line: Count the up days. A euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 is the short setup.

wrong.A drive; buy the 5-minute high: A euphoric drive on day 3 to 5 of a burst is the short setup, not a long.
wrong.A drive at half size: Half size on a climax is still a long into the top.

questions.q: Your view?
questions.story: A leader gaps up and climbs at a steady slope. The candles shrink and price hugs its short-term average. A friend wants to short the strength.
choices: Do not fade a steady drive
Short the first red candle
Short at the first bar's high
questions.answer: Do not fade a steady drive
questions.why: Do not fade it. A consistent slope and shrinking candles are a steady trend, and Breitstein says losses from fighting that trend were entirely avoidable.
questions.lesson_line: A steady drive is a trend to respect. Fading it is the avoidable loss.

wrong.Short the first red candle: In a steady drive a red candle is a pause, not a reversal. Fading it is the mistake.
wrong.Short at the first bar's high: That is where the drive buys. Selling there fights the trend.

questions.q: Add?
questions.story: Your drive is up 1R at 9:50. The stock looks like it is trending, and you want to add size.
choices: Yes; add half on the first dip
Yes; add a third at 2R
No; full size at one price
questions.answer: No; full size at one price
questions.why: No. Full size at one price with one stop, no adding. SMB: we do not trust trends in the first 30 minutes.
questions.lesson_line: A drive is not yet a trend. Full size at one price, no adding.

wrong.Yes; add half on the first dip: Adding to a drive in the first 30 minutes mistakes a drive for a trend.
wrong.Yes; add a third at 2R: No adding at all. One price, one stop.

questions.q: Which grades higher?
questions.story: Two drives on the same daily setup. One's first bar runs 1.6x its normal volume. The other runs 5.3x and trades its average daily volume by 9:45.
choices: They grade the same
The 5.3x drive
The 1.6x drive
questions.why: The 5.3x drive. Average daily volume traded within the first 15 to 30 minutes is an A+ mark. CNC's 5.3x was the heaviest first bar in our set.
questions.lesson_line: Heavier first-bar volume and a full day's average by 9:45 grade the drive up.

wrong.The 1.6x drive: The lighter drive lacks the A+ volume marks.
wrong.They grade the same: Volume grades the drive. The 5.3x one earns the A+ mark.

questions.q: What was this loss?
questions.story: TSEM, 2026-09-17: you buy a drive at 216.48 with the stop at 214.23. It reaches 2.1R by 9:50, then falls through its open and takes the stop.
choices: A reason to widen the stop next time
The plan working; a 1R loss
A broken rule; the stop was too tight
A reason to re-enter at once
questions.why: The plan working. The stop sat under the day's low, where the rule puts it, and the loss was 1R. A tight stop is not a free stop, and a stop-out is not a re-entry without a new trigger.
questions.lesson_line: The stop under the day's low keeps every loss at 1R. A stop-out is the plan, not a mistake.

wrong.A broken rule; the stop was too tight: The stop sat a few cents under the day's low, as the rule says. The rule was followed.
wrong.A reason to re-enter at once: After a stop-out we buy again only on a new trigger.
wrong.A reason to widen the stop next time: The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.q: What do you do?
questions.story: EAT, 2026-09-22: you bought at 9:40. The high prints at 9:45, a lower high follows, and at 9:55 the first close under VWAP comes.
choices: Hold; the stop is the exit
Sell at once at the market
Add on the dip
Widen the stop
questions.answer: Hold; the stop is the exit
questions.why: Hold. Losing VWAP after the entry is a warning, and the stop is the exit. EAT took the stop at 14:20 and closed at 24% of its range. The loss was planned.
questions.lesson_line: A lost VWAP after you buy is a warning. The stop does the selling.

wrong.Sell at once at the market: After the entry it is a warning only. The stop is the only exit.
wrong.Add on the dip: Full size at one price, no adding. Adding into a failing drive is the worst version.
wrong.Widen the stop: The stop only moves up, never wider.

questions.q: Buy again?
questions.story: PAYC, 2026-10-01: you buy at 9:35 and the fill is the high of the day. It slides and takes the stop at 10:35, then bounces for the rest of the day.
choices: Yes; the stop-out was a fluke
Yes, with a wider stop this time
No; never trade it this month
Only on a new trigger and new stop
questions.answer: Only on a new trigger and new stop
questions.why: Only on a new trigger. After a stop-out we buy again only on a new trigger, as a new trade with its own stop and every rule.
questions.lesson_line: A stop-out is not a re-entry. A new trigger is a new trade with its own stop.

wrong.Yes; the stop-out was a fluke: A bounce is not a trigger. A new trade needs its own trigger.
wrong.Yes, with a wider stop this time: The stop only moves up, never wider, and a new trade needs a new trigger first.
wrong.No; never trade it this month: A new trigger is allowed. It counts against 3 tries a week and 6 a month.

questions.q: What do you take?
questions.story: The market reads Red. At 9:35 four drives fire at once, each with a clean first bar and heavy volume.
choices: Zero; Red is mostly cash
The best one, at half size
All four; the setups are clean
questions.why: Zero. In Red it is mostly cash, however clean the drive. On 2026-10-06 four strict drives fired and all were stopped: the drives were real for five minutes and the market was not.
questions.lesson_line: Read the market first. A clean drive in a Red market is a loss waiting to happen.

wrong.The best one, at half size: Red is mostly cash. Half size is still a long in a Red market.
wrong.All four; the setups are clean: Clean setups do not beat a Red market. On 2026-10-06 all four were stopped.

questions.q: In our 12-week scan, 41 drives passed every rule. About how many were stopped on the drive day?
choices: About nine in ten
About four in ten
About one in ten
Almost none
questions.why: About four in ten. Many drives that pass every rule fail fast: 87.8% were stopped within 20 sessions and 41.5% on the drive day itself.
questions.lesson_line: Plan on losing often. A drive that keeps going pays in minutes; one that does not is over by 10:00.

wrong.About one in ten: Far more fail on the day. 41.5% were stopped on the drive day.
wrong.Almost none: A drive that fails is over by 10:00, and many do.
wrong.About nine in ten: 87.8% were stopped within 20 sessions, not on the drive day.

questions.q: What is the entry?
questions.story: You missed the 9:35 break. At 10:45 the stock pulls back on lighter volume, holds VWAP and stays above the first bar's high.
choices: Skip; a missed 9:35 break is gone
A break over the pullback's high
Market now, stop under the low
questions.answer: A break over the pullback's high
questions.why: The break back over the pullback's high, with the stop a few cents under the pullback's low. That is the second entry.
questions.lesson_line: Wait for the pullback to prove itself, then buy its break. The stop is under the pullback low.

wrong.Skip; a missed 9:35 break is gone: A first pullback that holds VWAP is the second entry. The setup is still on.
wrong.Market now, stop under the low: The second entry buys the break back over the pullback's high, not a market order mid-pullback.

questions.q: A gap up that drives the day after a burst down can be taken below the 200-day. That is the Parabolic Long's entry, not this card's.
questions.why: True. The rulebook allows a parabolic long below the 200-day. That drive is the Parabolic Long's entry, not the opening drive's.
questions.lesson_line: The 200-day has one exception, and it belongs to the Parabolic Long.

questions.q: Write the plan: entry, stop, first trim.
questions.story: LRCX, 2026-09-18: a leader, RS 82, above its 200-day. The first 5-minute bar runs 272.80 to 277.23 on 5.7x volume.
choices: Limit 275.00; stop 268.00; out at 2R
Market at 9:40 close; stop 272.80; hold
Market 277.24; stop 272.75; third at 3R
questions.why: Market at 277.24, stop 272.75, a third at 3R. A market order as it trades through, a few cents under the day's low, the first third at 3R. LRCX reached 3R at the next open.
questions.lesson_line: Entry, stop, trim, trail. Write it before the open and execute it without a debate.

wrong.Limit 275.00; stop 268.00; out at 2R: A limit under the first bar's high never fills on the break. A stop down at 268.00 is nowhere near the day's low.
wrong.Market at 9:40 close; stop 272.80; hold: The trigger is the trade through, not the close, and the stop sits under the low, not on it.

questions.q: What does the gap rule say?
questions.story: SANM, 2026-09-11: you bought at 208.00 with the stop at 205.66 and sold a third at 3R. On 09-14 the stock gaps down through the stop.
choices: Buy more at the lower price
30-minute low is the stop; cap at 2R
Sell at the open, no questions
Hold; the third banked covers it
questions.answer: 30-minute low is the stop; cap at 2R
questions.why: The first 30-minute low is the new stop, and if the first 30 minutes take the loss past 2R, get out. The third sold at 3R was already banked.
questions.lesson_line: A gap through the stop is the one exception. The first 30 minutes decide, under a 2R cap.

wrong.Sell at the open, no questions: The gap rule gives the first 30 minutes the decision, under the 2R cap.
wrong.Hold; the third banked covers it: The banked third does not move the stop. The 30-minute low does.
wrong.Buy more at the lower price: Full size at one price with one stop, no adding.

questions.q: Fill 208.00, stop 205.66. A gap-down day opens below the stop. At what price is the loss 2R?
questions.why: 203.32. One R is the fill minus the stop; subtract two of those from the fill. If the first 30 minutes take the loss past that price, get out.
questions.lesson_line: Know the 2R price before the gap. The first 30-minute low must stay above it.

questions.q: SMB Capital scalps the drive with its own exits. Ours is a third at 3R, a third at 5R and a trail, because we swing trade.
questions.why: True. SMB's scalp exits are not ours. We swing trade, so the drive is held under the house trims and the trail.
questions.lesson_line: Borrow the entry, not the exit. Our trims are 3R and 5R, then the trail.

questions.q: The SMB Capital desk says you are in a scalp or a hold plan. What is the mistake?
choices: Using a stop on a scalp
Taking a profit at all
Switching plans mid-trade
Choosing the plan before the entry
questions.why: Switching plans mid-trade, from a hold to a scalp or back. The plan is chosen before the entry and kept.
questions.lesson_line: Pick the plan before you buy. Changing it mid-trade is the mistake.

wrong.Choosing the plan before the entry: That is the point. SMB says to choose the plan before entry.
wrong.Using a stop on a scalp: Every plan has a stop. It is a real order with the broker.
wrong.Taking a profit at all: Profits are the aim. We trim to bank them.

questions.q: Where is the first trim taken?
questions.story: You hold a drive with the first trim at 3R. The next morning the stock opens above 3R.
choices: At the first 30-minute low
At the open; the level is passed
At the old 3R price, with a limit
Wait for it to come back
questions.answer: At the open; the level is passed
questions.why: At the open. If a stock opens above a trim level, take the trim at the open. LRCX and STX reached 3R at the next session's open.
questions.lesson_line: A level the day opens past is taken at the open. Do not wait for a price that is gone.

wrong.At the old 3R price, with a limit: That price is behind you. The trim is taken at the open.
wrong.Wait for it to come back: Waiting for a level that has passed is hope, not a rule.
wrong.At the first 30-minute low: That is the gap-down stop rule. This is a gap up through a trim.

questions.q: A drive fills at 96.97. Its 10-day average is 88.31. How far is the fill above the 10-day, in percent?
questions.why: 9.81%, just inside the 10% line. That is MXL's case: 9.8% over its 10-day, the edge of the stretch rule, and it ran 5.2R at its best.
questions.lesson_line: Measure the stretch against the 10-day. Past 10% over, the long is skipped.

questions.q: A stock's average daily volume is 850,000 shares. What is the most we would own, in shares?
questions.why: 8,500 shares. We never own more than 1% of a stock's average daily volume.
questions.lesson_line: Size to the volume. One percent of the average day is the ceiling.

questions.q: What do you take?
questions.story: Your list shows six drive candidates, and the market reads Orange.
choices: Only the A+ drives
All six; each has a clean setup
None; Orange is Red
questions.why: Only the A+ drives. Orange is A+ setups only. A clean first bar is not the same as an A+ drive.
questions.lesson_line: Orange means A+ only. Cut the list to the best before the open.

wrong.All six; each has a clean setup: Orange allows A+ setups only. Clean is not the same as A+.
wrong.None; Orange is Red: Red is mostly cash. Orange still allows the A+ drives.
